n37e14db2a85.s:
Consider the following statements about the Quit India Movement in Andhra:
1. The Madras–Puri passenger train was burnt at Tenali after police firing on 12 August 1942.
2. The police firing at Bhimavaram came before the firing at Tenali.
3. Guntur saw police firing on 13 August 1942.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n37e14db2a85.x: Tenali (12 August, train burnt) and Guntur (13 August) are correct; Bhimavaram's firing was on 17 August, after Tenali.

n902aefd92a8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Pattabhi Sitaramayya during the Quit India Movement?
o: He was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort.
He wrote the diary 'Feathers and Stones' in prison.
He wrote 'Feathers and Stones' in Vellore Central Jail.
He was a member of the Congress Working Committee.
n902aefd92a8.x: He was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort and wrote 'Feathers and Stones' there, not at Vellore.

nindian-history-113-14.s: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'?
nindian-history-113-14.x: The slogan was Bose's; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's, 'Do or Die' Gandhi's and 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' Shastri's.

n46de21055ce.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra leaders during the Quit India Movement?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a CWC member, was jailed along with the CWC.
Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground throughout.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
The secret paper 'Quit India' spread the pamphlet 'Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi'.
n46de21055ce.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed again in 1942, not for the first time.

new.s: When did the Congress provincial ministries resign in protest against India's entry into World War II?
new.x: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939; December 1939 was the Day of Deliverance and March 1940 the Ramgarh session.

new.s: Why did the Congress ministries resign in 1939?
o: The August Offer gave the minorities a veto
India was declared a party to World War II without consulting Indians
The Cripps proposals allowed provinces to opt out
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance
new.x: Linlithgow declared India a party to the war without consulting Indians, so the ministries resigned; the August Offer and Cripps came later.

new.s: The Ramgarh session of the Congress held in March 1940 was its:
new.x: Ramgarh (Bihar), March 1940, was the 53rd Congress session.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramgarh session of the Congress:
1. It was held in March 1940 in Bihar.
2. It was held after the August Offer.
3. It offered war help if a provisional national government was formed at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ramgarh (March 1940) came before the August Offer (August 1940), which was the reply to it; statements 1 and 3 are correct.

new.s: Who said Dominion Status was 'dead as a doornail' while rejecting the August Offer?
new.x: Nehru dismissed the August Offer's Dominion Status as 'dead as a doornail'.

new.s: The demand for a Constituent Assembly was first raised in 1934 by:
new.x: M.N. Roy first raised the demand in 1934; the Congress adopted it in 1935.

new.s: On which date did Lord Linlithgow make the August Offer?
new.x: The August Offer was made on 8 August 1940; 8 August 1942 was the Quit India resolution.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Individual Satyagraha?
o: It started from Paunar near Wardha
Its aim was mass mobilisation against British rule
Chosen individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest
new.x: Individual Satyagraha aimed at asserting freedom of speech against the war, not mass mobilisation, hence 'limited'.

new.s: Brahma Dutt was chosen as the third satyagrahi of the Individual Satyagraha mainly for his:
new.x: Brahma Dutt was chosen for moral conviction, not political prominence; Bihar's leader was Shyam Narayan Singh.

new.s: Which Andhra municipality passed a resolution condemning the arrests of Vinoba Bhave, Nehru and Patel in the Individual Satyagraha?
new.x: Ongole Municipality condemned the arrests of Vinoba, Nehru and Patel.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Individual Satyagraha:
1. The government arrested Vinoba Bhave, Nehru and Patel.
2. Ongole Municipality passed a resolution condemning these arrests.
3. Brahma Dutt was the second satyagrahi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Nehru was the second satyagrahi and Brahma Dutt the third.

new.s: In the Individual Satyagraha, Gandhi held it wrong to help the British war effort with:
new.x: Gandhi's line was: 'It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money.'

new.s: Apart from the Cripps Mission of 1942, Sir Stafford Cripps was also a member of the:
new.x: Cripps was also a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946.

new.s: Under the Cripps proposals, provincial lower houses were to elect the constitution-making body at what share of their size?
new.x: The provincial lower houses were to act as an electoral college of 1/10th of their size, by proportional representation.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the Cripps proposals?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to Indian hands
Indian Union with Dominion Status after the war
Right to secede from the Commonwealth
Nominees of princely states in the constitution-making body
new.x: Defence and the army were to stay with the British in the interim; the rest were in the draft declaration.

new.s: Which British offer was the first to allow provinces to stay outside the Indian Union?
new.x: The Cripps proposals were the first to allow a provincial opt-out, conceding Pakistan in principle.

new.s: Gandhi described the Cripps offer as a:
new.x: Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque', popularly quoted with 'on a crashing bank'.

new.s: Who was the Congress President during the Cripps negotiations of 1942?
new.x: Azad, then Congress President, negotiated with Cripps along with Nehru.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the rejection of the Cripps proposals:
1. The Congress feared the Balkanisation of India.
2. The Muslim League opposed a single Indian Union.
3. The Muslim League accepted them because Pakistan was explicitly granted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both rejected the proposals; the League did so because Pakistan was not explicitly granted and it opposed a single Union.

new.s: The 'take it or leave it' attitude cited among the causes of the Cripps Mission's failure was that of:
new.x: Cripps's 'take it or leave it' attitude, along with Churchill's sabotage, made the talks break down.

new.s: In which month and year was the Wavell Plan announced, leading to the Simla Conference?
new.x: The Wavell Plan came on 14 June 1945; the Desai-Liaquat Pact was in January 1945.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Desai-Liaquat Pact
2. Wavell Plan
3. Arrival of Lord Wavell as Viceroy
4. Cripps Mission
new.x: Cripps Mission (March 1942), Wavell arrives (October 1943), Desai-Liaquat Pact (January 1945), Wavell Plan (June 1945).

new.s: Lord Wavell arrived as Viceroy of India in:
new.x: Wavell arrived as Viceroy in October 1943.

new.s: During the Cripps Mission, rumours spread of Japanese bombing of which Andhra towns?
new.x: Rumours of Japanese bombing of Vizag and Kakinada spread during the Cripps Mission.

new.s: In April 1942 Gandhi used the phrase 'Quit India' in his paper:
new.x: Gandhi used 'Quit India' in Harijan in April 1942.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of the Quit India Movement:
1. The failure of the Cripps Mission was the main trigger.
2. Rangoon fell to Japan in March 1942.
3. Rising prices and wartime shortages added to the discontent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are causes: Cripps's failure, the Japanese advance in the East and economic grievances.

new.s: Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, where the Quit India resolution was ratified, is now known as:
new.x: Gowalia Tank Maidan is now August Kranti Ground.

new.s: The Quit India resolution moved by Nehru was seconded by:
new.x: At Wardha and at Bombay, Nehru moved the resolution and Sardar Patel seconded it.

new.s: The resolution passed by the Congress Working Committee on 14 July 1942 is known as the:
new.x: The CWC resolution at Wardha (14 July) is the Wardha Resolution; the AICC ratification on 8 August is the August Resolution.

new.s: Which pair of group and Gandhi's Quit India instruction is correctly matched?
o: Soldiers – Not to fire on Indians
Students – Not to fire on Indians
Soldiers – Pledge loyalty to Congress while in service
new.x: Soldiers were told not to fire on Indians; government servants to stay in service pledging loyalty to Congress; students that they may leave studies.

new.s: 'Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight' was said by:
new.x: The words are Gandhi's, from the Quit India phase, not Tagore's.

new.s: The slogan 'Back to the Vedas' was given by:
new.x: 'Back to the Vedas' was Dayanand Saraswati's (Arya Samaj); C.R. Das gave 'Swaraj for the masses'.

new.s: Who called British rule 'the political symptom of our social disease'?
new.x: Tagore described British rule as the political symptom of our social disease.

new.s: Who said, 'Everything could wait but not agriculture'?
new.x: Nehru said it about post-Independence agriculture; Shastri gave 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan'.

new.s: Where was Gandhi detained after his arrest in August 1942?
new.x: Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace, Poona; the CWC members were held at Ahmednagar Fort.

new.s: Gandhi's 21-day fast of February 1943 led to the resignation of:
o: three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council
new.x: Three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigned; Baldev Sahai had resigned in 1942 over the arrests.

new.s: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention at Poona in:
new.x: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention at Poona in 1944.

new.s: The brothers Gangaram and Kheemdev were killed in police firing during the Quit India Movement at:
new.x: Gangaram and Kheemdev were killed in police firing at Almora.

new.s: On which date did Jayaprakash Narayan escape from Hazaribagh Jail?
new.x: JP escaped on Diwali, 9 November 1942, with Yogendra Shukla.

new.s: Which pair of underground leader and activity is correctly matched?
o: Ram Manohar Lohia – Formed the Azad Dasta
Aruna Asaf Ali – Escaped Hazaribagh Jail
Jayaprakash Narayan – Hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank
Usha Mehta – Ran the secret Congress Radio
new.x: Usha Mehta ran Congress Radio; JP formed the Azad Dasta and escaped Hazaribagh; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag; Lohia broadcast on the radio.

new.s: Where did Jayaprakash Narayan declare 'Sampoorna Kranti' on 5 June 1974?
new.x: JP declared Sampoorna Kranti at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on 5 June 1974.

new.s: What was Sucheta Kripalani's role in the Quit India Movement?
o: She ran the secret Congress Radio
She organised the underground movement while in hiding
She hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank
She led the Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
new.x: Sucheta Kripalani went into hiding as an organiser of the underground movement and was arrested in 1944.

new.s: Matangini Hazra fell in police firing while leading a procession at:
new.x: Matangini Hazra fell at Tamluk, Bengal; Kanaklata Barua at Gohpur, Assam.

new.s: How old was Matangini Hazra when she fell in police firing in 1942?
new.x: Matangini Hazra was 73 years old.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about women of the Quit India phase:
1. Kanaklata Barua was shot dead at Gohpur in Assam.
2. Shanti Ghosh was a leading organiser of the Quit India Movement.
3. Matangini Hazra led a procession at Tamluk in Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; Shanti Ghosh was a revolutionary of 1931, not linked to Quit India.

new.s: The 'Prati Sarkar' parallel government at Satara was led by:
new.x: Satara's Prati Sarkar was led by Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil; Chittu Pandey led Ballia.

new.s: Which was the longest-lasting parallel government of the Quit India phase?
new.x: Satara (mid-1943 to 1945) was the longest; Ballia (about a week) the shortest.

new.s: Talcher, where a parallel government was set up in 1942, is in:
new.x: Talcher is in Odisha.

new.s: Nyayadan Mandals (people's courts) were run by the parallel government at:
new.x: Satara's Prati Sarkar ran Nyayadan Mandals, village libraries and prohibition.

new.s: At which Andhra town was the Collectorate attacked after police firing on 17 August 1942?
new.x: Bhimavaram saw firing on 17 August and an attack on the Collectorate.

new.s: During the Quit India Movement, lawyers of which Andhra town demanded Gandhi's release?
new.x: Kakinada's lawyers demanded Gandhi's release.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the attitude of parties to the Quit India Movement:
1. The ban on the CPI was lifted on 23 July 1942.
2. The Unionist Party of Punjab supported the movement.
3. The Muslim League under Jinnah condemned the movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Unionist Party was among those that did not support it.

new.s: How did the Muslim League under Jinnah respond to the Quit India Movement?
new.x: Jinnah and the League condemned it, and the British and Muslims came closer.

new.s: In which year did the Congress ministries resign, leading to the limited Individual Satyagraha?
new.x: The Congress ministries resigned in November 1939, which led to the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41:
1. Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi.
2. Jawaharlal Nehru was the third satyagrahi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vinoba Bhave was first; Nehru was the second, not the third.

new.s: R.P.G.V. Govindan Chettiyar, honoured in June 2025 under Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, was jailed for six months in the:
new.x: The Tamil Nadu freedom fighter was jailed for six months in the Individual Satyagraha.

new.s: On which date was the AICC session at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, that gave the 'Do or Die' call held?
new.x: The AICC met on 8 August 1942, not 6 August; 29 July was the Andhra Circular and 14 July the Wardha CWC.

new.s: Who was taken to the Aga Khan Palace, Pune, along with Gandhi on 9 August 1942?
new.x: Gandhi was taken to the Aga Khan Palace with Sarojini Naidu; Pattabhi Sitaramayya went with the CWC to Ahmednagar Fort.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra (Kurnool) Circular:
1. It was dated 29 July 1942.
2. It was issued after the Bombay AICC session.
3. It gave directives for the coming movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It was dated 29 July 1942, before the 8 August AICC, and gave an action programme; statements 1 and 3 are correct.

new.s: The Andhra Circular came to be called the 'Kurnool Circular' because it was:
o: adopted by an AICC session at Kurnool
drafted by Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool
read out at a Kurnool public meeting by Gandhi
seized by the police at Kurnool
new.x: The circular was seized by the police at Kurnool, hence the name; its author was Kala Venkata Rao.

new.s: The APCC meeting at Machilipatnam during the Quit India Movement was held under:
new.x: The APCC met at Machilipatnam under Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

new.s: How many students marched to the Sub-Magistrate's court at Chirala on 12 August 1942 to close it?
new.x: About 500 students marched to the Sub-Magistrate's court at Chirala.

new.s: Bhimavaram, where police fired on 17 August 1942, is in which district?
new.x: Bhimavaram is in West Godavari; Kakinada is in East Godavari.

new.s: Which pair of Andhra place and Quit India event is correctly matched?
o: Bhimavaram – Lawyers' resolution for Gandhi's release
new.x: Bapatla's railway station was burnt; Bhimavaram had the 17 August firing, Kakinada the lawyers' resolution and Tenali the train burning.

new.s:
Arrange the police firings of August 1942 in Andhra in chronological order:
1. Bhimavaram
2. Tenali
3. Guntur
new.x: Tenali (12 August), Guntur (13 August), Bhimavaram (17 August).

new.s: Tenali, where police firing on 12 August 1942 killed about nine people, is in which district?
new.x: Tenali is in Guntur district.

new.s: Who wrote the song 'Paradesiyulu tolagandi...' during the Quit India Movement?
new.x: The song was by Vanamamalai Varadacharyulu; Karunasree contributed a poem.

new.s: Which Kurnool leader stayed underground throughout the Quit India Movement?
new.x: Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah stayed underground; Pattabhi and Unnava were jailed and Annapurna Devi arrested.

new.s: Chitturi Annapurna Devi was arrested in 1942 for pamphlets and picketing at:
new.x: Annapurna Devi was arrested at Guntur; Duvvuri Subbamma faced the lathi charge at Peddapuram.

new.s: Duvvuri Subbamma faced a lathi charge during the Quit India Movement at:
new.x: Duvvuri Subbamma faced the lathi charge at Peddapuram.

new.s: How old was Chitturi Annapurna Devi when she was arrested at Guntur in 1942?
new.x: Chitturi Annapurna Devi was 17.

new.s: After opposing Quit India, which Communist was the only one to win from Andhra in the 1945 elections?
new.x: Only Pillalamarri Venkateswara Rao won from Andhra in 1945; Chandra Rajeswara Rao was secretary of the 1943 conference.

new.s: The Third Communist Conference held at Vijayawada in 1943 is notable as:
o: the first open Communist conference in Andhra
the meeting that adopted the Kurnool Circular
the conference that launched Quit India in Andhra
the last conference before the CPI ban
new.x: It was the first open Communist conference in Andhra, after the ban was lifted in July 1942.
